title: OPA in Production
subtitle: Bundles, data injection, REST, and hot reload
content:
📦 From Files to Bundles

Real estates do not PUT Rego through ad-hoc REST calls (the demo-repos do that for teaching). Production: .rego + data.json in Git → CI (opa fmt, opa test) → signed bundle → OPA sidecars poll/push. Hot reload lands in under a second with zero restarts — the rest-rego sidecar demonstrates exactly this.

OPA production loop: fmt, test, bundle, inject data 
# CI gate for every policy change (copy into your pipeline)
opa fmt --diff ./policies        # canonical formatting, diff fails the build
opa test ./policies/ -v          # allow-tests + deny-tests + regression tests
opa build -b ./policies -o bundle.tar.gz   # ship one artifact

# Data injection at runtime (roles WITHOUT redeploying policy):
# PUT /v1/data/user_roles/alice  ["analyst"]
# PATCH /v1/data/cnapp/rbac  [{"op":"add","path":"/blacklist/...","value":{...}}]
# CI gate for every policy change (copy into your pipeline) opa fmt --diff ./policies # canonical formatting, diff fails the build opa test ./policies/ -v # allow-tests + deny-tests + regression tests opa build -b ./policies -o bundle.tar.gz # ship one artifact # Data injection at runtime (roles WITHOUT redeploying policy): # PUT /v1/data/user_roles/alice ["analyst"] # PATCH /v1/data/cnapp/rbac [{"op":"add","path":"/blacklist/...","value":{...}}]

📨 Decision API, Precisely

Package app.rbac is queried at POST /v1/data/app/rbac with {"input": {...}} — the wrapper key is mandatory and the #1 beginner 404/undefined cause in every demo repo. Query a sub-rule (/v1/data/demo/allow) for booleans, or the package path for the full decision document.

Decision call: input wrapper + package-derived path 
curl -s -X POST localhost:8181/v1/data/demo/allow \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "input": { "method": "PUT", "path": "/teams/123",
                   "roles": ["analyst"], "groups": ["Team123"] } }'
# -> {"result": true}   (team rule matched; Team999 would return false)
curl -s -X POST localhost:8181/v1/data/demo/allow \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "input": { "method": "PUT", "path": "/teams/123", "roles": ["analyst"], "groups": ["Team123"] } }' # -> {"result": true} (team rule matched; Team999 would return false)

🔍 Critical Review: Production Gaps the Demos Admit

  • Debug with reasons: the zero-trust gatekeeper repo queries a companion data.zt.authz.reasons rule to name the vetoing sub-policy. Ship a reasons rule from day one.
  • Decision logs: OPA can ship every decision (input + result + policy id) to your log pipeline — the audit trail compliance asked for in Lesson 5.
  • Cache carefully: the Keycloak-middleware pattern caches decisions ~5s with OPA_FAIL_OPEN=false. Cache keys must include tenant + roles + resource, or you will serve alice's verdict to bob.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Compare sidecar vs gateway vs middleware latency and failure posture. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: What is the production path for a policy change?

options.text: Git → opa fmt/test in CI → bundle → sidecars hot-reload
SSH into servers and edit Rego by hand
PUT the policy via ad-hoc REST calls in production

questions.explanation: Policy-as-code earns its name: reviewed, tested, bundled, distributed. Ad-hoc REST PUTs are for learning, not for prod.

questions.question: POST /v1/data/demo/allow with a bare input (no input wrapper key). What happens?

options.text: Rules see empty input and deny (or misbehave) — the wrapper is mandatory

questions.explanation: Every demo repo calls this out: runtime facts must sit under input. Missing wrapper is the classic 'policy works in playground, denies in prod' bug.

questions.question: Alice's admin role is revoked. Fastest correct propagation without redeploying policy?

options.text: PUT /v1/data/user_roles/alice with the new role list (data injection)
Rewrite and redeploy all Rego files
Wait for the JWT to expire someday

questions.explanation: Data (who-has-what-role) is separate from policy (what-roles-mean) precisely so revocation is a data write, demonstrated in the REST demo repos.

questions.question: A denial reaches your on-call with no explanation. What should have existed?

options.text: A reasons rule + decision logs naming the determining policy
More permissive rules so denials never happen
Deleting the logs to save disk

questions.explanation: The gatekeeper repo's reasons rule is the pattern: every deny carries its cause; decision logs preserve input+result for audit.

questions.question: You cache PDP decisions. What must the cache key include?

options.text: Subject identity/roles + tenant + action + resource (+ relevant context)

questions.explanation: Under-keyed caches serve one user's verdict to another — a cache-shaped authZ bypass. Key everything the decision depends on; TTL in seconds.

questions.question: You query /v1/data/app instead of /v1/data/app/allow. Difference?

options.text: Full decision document vs boolean — document for audit, boolean for the hot path

questions.explanation: Package path returns the whole document (reasons, obligations); sub-rule path returns the boolean. Choose per consumer.

questions.question: Decision logs must exclude PII but preserve cause. How?

options.text: Log inputs selectively (drop raw claims) plus determining policy ids and reason codes

questions.explanation: Auditability and privacy compose: keep the why (policy ids, reasons), drop the who (raw claims).

questions.question: Two sidecars run bundle v41 and v42 during rollout. Risk?

options.text: Verdict skew across instances — pin versions, roll forward fast, monitor diff rate

questions.explanation: Mixed-version fleets answer the same question differently. Bundle rollout is a deployment like any other.
